messages:
maria: heads up — saw a weird traffic split during the eu rollout. platinum customers in eu-west were routed to the older variant, not the canary A variant. looks like region affinity + cost-fallback logic overrode the per-tier rollout scope.
jon: hmm can you paste the request id / trace?
maria: trace 01H9ZQY4X2G-164, sample: 10.23.45.8 -> routed to variant:v1.2 (fallback). our rollout config had platinum in canary A at 20% for eu-west.
sasha: possible cause: routing precedence checks current availability/cost before evaluating rollout slices. config snippet from routing service:```json
{"steps": ["capacity_check","cost_preference","variant_selection","rollout_scope"]}
```
jon: that order is wrong for per-tier canaries. rollout_scope should be before cost_preference. otherwise cheap fallback masks targeted exposures.
kevin: agreed. quick thought: change to ["capacity_check","rollout_scope","variant_selection","cost_preference"] and make cost_preference only apply when rollout_scope doesn't match any variant.
product-ana: from a UX POV we also need console visibility — the rollout page should show when cost-fallback suppressed a slice. customers will ask why platinum didn't see canary. add a telemetry tag like rollout.blocked_by_fallback.
maria: +1. we lost 8 platinum samples during the 2h window, which skewed the metric delta.
jon: any safety concerns making that precedence change? i.e. could it cause hotspots on expensive variants?
kevin: we still honor capacity_check first so we won't route into an overloaded pool. the change only ensures enrollment into scoped rollouts if capacity is available. cost_preference then picks cheapest variant among allowed ones for non-scoped traffic.
sasha: I'll open a tiny patch to the routing lib. patch:```diff
- steps = ["capacity_check","cost_preference","variant_selection","rollout_scope"]
+ steps = ["capacity_check","rollout_scope","variant_selection","cost_preference"]
```
maria: nice. can we also add a quick integration test that simulates platinum eu-west and verifies enrolment to canary A when capacity ok?
kevin: yes — test matrix: tier={free,pro,platinum}, region={eu-west,us-east}, capacity ok/low -> assert rollout enrollment matches scope first.
product-ana: and add console flag to surface when cost_preference fired as a fallback, label it 'used_fallback:cost'. designers will add tooltip.
deploy-bot: rollout-change job started by sasha at 1998884200 — running canary of routing change in staging.
sasha: rolled out to staging, running simulation load now. logs look good, platinum samples get canary as expected.
maria: can we get a telemetry event name? i'll add to the eval dashboard.
product-ana: event: routing.rollout_scope_enforced and routing.rollout_cost_fallback_used. include fields: tenant_tier, region, request_id, chosen_variant.
jon: ok let's ship to prod tomorrow after a short soak. who owns the console flag?
product-ana: i'll own the console bits, sasha owns routing lib, kevin owns tests and infra gating.
kensmith: @channel quick note — remember to update runbooks if this changes incident signals for variant pressure :eyes:.
maria: thanks everyone. capturing action items: 1) sasha: patch + prod rollout, 2) kevin: tests and canary gating, 3) product-ana: console telemetry and flag. back to sync after prod soak. :thumbsup:
